description: Seed capability vocabulary. Extend per project; do not treat this as a fixed list of roles.
resolution_policy: A general-purpose language model is one reasoning provider, not the whole execution system.
Treat a capability as available only when the current host/project can actually exercise it with evidence at the reliability required by the task; verbal confidence is not capability proof.
Prefer deterministic project tools, runtime evidence, browser/API access, existing Skills, connected services, and independent acceptance signals before adding another general model or runtime.

When a consequential result needs independence, choose an evidence path with a meaningfully different failure mode from the builder; this may be deterministic tests, browser/runtime observation, a calibrated evaluator, a bounded specialist, or a different model/provider when semantic judgment itself is the gap.
Only a proven unresolved capability gap justifies adding a new provider, and the added provider must be verified against the original gap rather than merely installed.

project-discovery.description: Understand repository intent, architecture, state, constraints, tests, deployment and unresolved risks.

requirement-reasoning.description: Resolve requested outcome, deliverables, constraints, decision boundaries and acceptance evidence while preserving domain/lived evidence that the person may hold even when they cannot express it in software vocabulary.

architecture-design.description: Design or evaluate system boundaries, interfaces, data flow and trade-offs.

implementation.description: Modify project artifacts or code to realize the accepted design.

repository-operations.description: Inspect history/issues/PRs and perform authorized branch, commit, PR or merge operations.

browser-validation.description: Observe rendered behavior and exercise user flows in a real or automated browser.

data-access.description: Read or query project-relevant databases, analytics or structured data with least privilege.

security-review.description: Review changes for security boundaries, secrets, unsafe dependencies and abuse paths.

verification.description: Define and execute evidence that the requested outcome works and regressions are controlled, using an acceptance path credible enough for the claim rather than builder self-assertion alone.

release-validation.description: Verify build/release/deployment state without assuming implementation implies deployability.

research.description: Gather, compare and synthesize reliable external or internal evidence for a question.

document-production.description: Create or transform structured human-facing artifacts while preserving source intent.
